text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - German Bunds and futures were down and near the day's lows in late dealings on Thursday, hurt by profit-taking and slightly lower U.S. debt markets. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.45, down 0.23 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts and short sterling futures were slammed by above-expectation inflation figures and an article by Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke saying it was uncertain if he or Bank of England Governor Eddie George was right about rates. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-13/32, down 22/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures settled weaker but well off the lows struck as the market took a breather from five successive days on the rise, with little sign spend-happy sentiment was likely to abate. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 126.42, down 0.12 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures recovered from early losses helped by the renewed strength of the lira, while comments by Bank of Italy governer Antonio Fazio were seen as supportive. Despite losses the general optimistic mood has not changed and traders expect the market to hold in current ranges. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 123.55, down 0.10 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - Prices of U.S. Treasury securities were lingering near session lows around midday after retreating earlier on surprisingly restrained jobless claims data. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-09/32, down 09/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.86 percent.
JAPAN - The cash and futures Japanese Goverment Bonds (JGB) markets are closed on Thursday for a national holiday. Trading will resume on Friday.

EUROBONDS - Eurobond activity slowed after a hectic pace the previous day. European currencies provided the focus. TMCC issued a 200 billion lire five-year bond. LVMH launched a 1.5 billion French franc six-year bond at 22 b.p. over government bonds. Petronas was due to price its three bonds for a total of $1.5 billion later today.
